[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (f) where—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (i) subparagraph (d)(i) or (iii) applies, there is only one claimant making the claim, and the claimant informs the court that there is only one defendant; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (ii) subparagraph (d)(ii) applies, the claim is brought by one claimant against either one or two defendants, or is brought by two claimants against one defendant;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (g). if an individual, the claimant is aged 18 years or older;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (h). the claimant is not a “protected party” (as defined);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (i) the claimant’s postal address for service is within –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (i) the United Kingdom if the claimant is acting in person;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (ii) England and Wales if the claimant is represented by a legal representative;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (j). the claimant has an email address which can be used for the case;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (k). Omitted

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (l). the claim is conducted in English, save that a party acting in person may view and complete screens, and submit the completed screens, in Welsh;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (m). the claimant does not have in force against them –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (1) “civil proceedings order” (as defined);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (2) an “all proceedings order” (as defined); or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (3)  “civil restraint order” (as defined);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (n). the claimant believes that the defendant–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (i). Omitted

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (ii). has a postal address for service within England and Wales;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (iii) if an individual, is aged 18 years or older;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (iv). is not a “protected party”(as defined); and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(3) A claim is only suitable for the pilot if all the following conditions are met–] (v). is not the Crown. ## 2.1(4) Omitted

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(4) Omitted] 2.1(5) If the claimant decides to use Online Civil Money Claims, this practice direction applies. Where provisions in this practice direction conflict with other provisions in the Civil Procedure Rules or other practice directions, this practice direction takes precedence until the claim is sent out of the pilot. Once the claim is sent out of the pilot, this practice direction will no longer apply. The rest of the Civil Procedure Rules and practice directions, however, will continue to apply to the claim, along with any changes to the Civil Procedure Rules or other practice directions made by this practice direction or orders made by the court to enable the claim to be sent out of the pilot successfully. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(4) Omitted] (5A) If all of the conditions in sub-paragraph (3) are met (or if all those conditions in sub-paragraph (3) would be met if the claimant’s and defendant’s representatives were registered with MyHMCTS), and the claim is not started using the procedure set out in either Practice Direction 7B or 7C or 51ZB—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(4) Omitted] (a) if the claimant’s legal representative is not registered with MyHMCTS they must register with MyHMCTS before the claim is started;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(4) Omitted] (b) the claimant must give the defendant the notice referred to in sub-paragraph (5C) unless it is impractical to do so; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(4) Omitted] (c) the claim must be started using the procedure set out in this Practice Direction. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(4) Omitted] (5B) If all of the conditions in sub-paragraph (5C) are met—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(4) Omitted] (a) if the defendant’s legal representative is not registered with MyHMCTS they must register with MyHMCTS before the claim is started;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(4) Omitted] (b) the defendant’s legal representative must—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(4) Omitted] (i) notify the claimant that they are instructed; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(4) Omitted] (ii) provide the claimant with their email address for claim notifications;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(4) Omitted] (c) the claimant must provide the defendant’s legal representative’s email address when completing the online claim form. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(4) Omitted] (5C) The conditions referred to in sub-paragraph (5B) are—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(4) Omitted] (a) the claimant gives the defendant at least 14 days’ notice of their intention to bring a claim under this Practice Direction; and (b) the defendant has instructed a legal representative before the claim is started. ## 2.1(6 ) Omitted

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2.1(6 ) Omitted] 2.1(7) Subject to sub-paragraphs (5A) to (5C), if both the claimant and the defendant are represented, but the defendant’s legal representative is not registered with MyHMCTS when the claim is issued, Sections 2A to 4 of this practice direction apply except, the claim will be sent out of Online Civil Money Claims as soon as it has been issued. ## SECTION 2A – PAYMENT OF COURT FEES

## Payment of court fees

## 2A.1-(1) Unless –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2A.1-(1) Unless –] (a) a party is acting in person; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2A.1-(1) Unless –] (b) they have made an application for Help with Fees,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2A.1-(1) Unless –] a party may only take a step using Online Civil Money Claims on payment of any relevant fee. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2A.1-(1) Unless –] (Relevant court fees are set out in the Civil Proceedings Fees Order 2008.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2A.1-(1) Unless –] (2) Court fees must be paid using any method permitted by HMCTS. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2A.1-(1) Unless –] (Civil Procedure Rule 3.7A1 provides that if the court fee for the trial or hearing to determine the substance of the claim is not paid on time, the claim is to be struck out automatically. Rule 3.7A1 also contains provisions about Help with Fees (as defined).)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2A.1-(1) Unless –] SECTION 2B – Fixed Costs

## 2B.1 (1) References in this Section to –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2B.1 (1) References in this Section to –] (a) “fixed commencement costs” means the commencement costs calculated by reference to the amount of the claim in accordance with Table 2 of CPR Practice Direction 45;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2B.1 (1) References in this Section to –] (b) judgment on an admission means judgment entered under paragraphs 7.4, 7.7, 7.40 and 7.41B;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2B.1 (1) References in this Section to –] (c) judgment in default means judgment entered pursuant to Section 11;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2B.1 (1) References in this Section to –] (d) a “Table” means a table in CPR Practice Direction 45. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2B.1 (1) References in this Section to –] (2) This Section applies where –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2B.1 (1) References in this Section to –] (a) judgment is entered in default or on an admission;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2B.1 (1) References in this Section to –] (b) the value of the claim exceeds £25; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2B.1 (1) References in this Section to –] (c) the claim form includes a claim for fixed commencement costs. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2B.1 (1) References in this Section to –] (3) Unless the court orders otherwise, the only costs allowed for the claimant’s legal representative’s charges and included in the judgment are the fixed commencement costs and—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2B.1 (1) References in this Section to –] (a) where judgment in default is entered, the relevant amount shown in Table 3 in the circumstances specified where judgment is entered in default of an acknowledgment of service under Civil Procedure Rule 12.4 (1); or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2B.1 (1) References in this Section to –] (b) where judgment on an admission is entered, the relevant amount shown in Table 3 in the circumstances specified where judgment is entered under Civil Procedure Rule 14.2 (5) (judgment on an admission of the whole or part of a claim for a specified sum) where the claimant accepts the defendant’s proposal as to the manner of payment. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 2B.1 (1) References in this Section to –] 2B.2. Where the defendant pays the money claimed within 28 days from the date of issue of the claim together with the court fee and, where the claimant is legally represented, fixed commencement costs included in the claim form, the defendant is not liable for any further costs unless the court orders otherwise. ## SECTION 3 – COURT TO KEEP THE PARTIES UPDATED ON THE PROGRESS OF THE PROCEEDINGS

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 3 – COURT TO KEEP THE PARTIES UPDATED ON THE PROGRESS OF THE PROCEEDINGS] Court to keep the parties updated on the progress of the proceedings

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 3 – COURT TO KEEP THE PARTIES UPDATED ON THE PROGRESS OF THE PROCEEDINGS] 3.1(1) When a party uses Online Civil Money Claims to take a formal step in relation to the claim, the court must keep a record of the fact the step has been taken, and of the date the step is recorded as taken. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 3 – COURT TO KEEP THE PARTIES UPDATED ON THE PROGRESS OF THE PROCEEDINGS] (2) The court must tell the party when it records the step as taken, and the date recorded. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 3 – COURT TO KEEP THE PARTIES UPDATED ON THE PROGRESS OF THE PROCEEDINGS] (3) The court must also tell the other parties if any step is recorded as taken, and the date of the step taken, unless the court has ordered or this practice direction provides that the other parties not be told. ## SECTION 4 – STARTING A CLAIM

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 4 – STARTING A CLAIM] Starting an online claim

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 4 – STARTING A CLAIM] 4.1(1) In order to start the process of making an online claim against another person, the claimant must –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 4 – STARTING A CLAIM] (a). complete the claim form using the relevant claim form screens, found on the OCMC website (“the online claim form”);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 4 – STARTING A CLAIM] (b) pay the appropriate fee that is prescribed in the Civil Proceedings Fees Order 2008 unless they have made an application for Help with Fees (as defined), and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 4 – STARTING A CLAIM] (c) submit the completed online claim form to the court using the OCMC website. ## 4.1(2) As part of completing the claim form, the claimant must –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 4.1(2) As part of completing the claim form, the claimant must –] (a) set out all the details about their claim that they want to rely on to support their claim; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 4.1(2) As part of completing the claim form, the claimant must –] (b) list any documents or other evidence that they may want to rely on to support their claim. ## 4.2 Making changes to the claim or response

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 4.2 Making changes to the claim or response] 4.2 If the claimant wants to amend their claim, or a defendant wants to amend their response, after their claim or response form (as appropriate) has been submitted, the claimant or defendant must make an application to the court. If the court receives such an application, it must refer the application to a judge for directions, which may include that the claim be sent out of Online Civil Money Claims. (Section 16B contains provisions about making applications.)

## 4.3 Issue and service of the claim to the claim form

## 4.3(1)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 4.3(1)] Unless the claimant is acting in person and–  (a) had made an application for Help with Fees; or  (b) has exercised the option to submit the claim in Welsh,  when the court receives a submitted claim form from the claimant and the fee for issuing the claim is paid in full, the court must issue the claim. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 4.3(1)] (1A) If the claimant is acting in person and has made an application for Help with Fees, the court must issue the claim only once the fee has been remitted, or in so far as it is not remitted, the fee for issuing the claim is paid in full. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 4.3(1)] (Section 4A contains provisions about the Welsh language, including submitting the claim in Welsh.)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 4.3(1)] 4.3(2) The court must notify the claimant when the online claim form has been issued and what the date of issue is. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 4.3(1)] 4.3(3) If the claim is one where paragraph 2.1(3)(d)(i) or (iii) applies, the court must serve the claim on the defendant, and sub-paragraphs (4) and (5) apply. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 4.3(1)] 4.3(4) The court serves the claim on the defendant by sending a paper version of the completed online claim form to the defendant at the postal address given for the defendant. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 4.3(1)] 4.3(5) At the same time that the court serves the claim form on the defendant, it must also notify them as to what the date of issue is. ## 4.3(6) If all parties are legally represented–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 4.3(6) If all parties are legally represented–] (a) the court is to use the OCMC website to–

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 4.3(6) If all parties are legally represented–] (i) serve the claim form on the defendant; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 4.3(6) If all parties are legally represented–] (ii) provide to the claimant a copy of the issued claim form; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 4.3(6) If all parties are legally represented–] (b) service of the claim form in accordance with subparagraph (a)(i) constitutes service of the claim form in accordance with Civil Procedure Rule 7.5(1). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 4.3(6) If all parties are legally represented–] (7) In all cases the claim is brought for the purpose of the Limitation Act 1980

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 4.3(6) If all parties are legally represented–] and any other period of limitation at the point at which the claim is issued, and not before. CPR Practice Direction 7A paragraph 6.1 does not apply. ## SECTION 4A – WELSH LANGUAGE – PARTIES ACTING IN PERSON

## Application of this Section

## 4A.1 This Section applies in relation to any party who is acting in person. ## Submission of claim in Welsh

## 4A.2 The claim must be issued in English, but if the claimant submitted the claim in

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 4A.2 The claim must be issued in English, but if the claimant submitted the claim in] Welsh, the court must issue the claim only once –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 4A.2 The claim must be issued in English, but if the claimant submitted the claim in] the court has sent the claim for translation into English and it has been translated; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 4A.2 The claim must be issued in English, but if the claimant submitted the claim in] the court has provided the translation to the claimant. ## Completion of screens in Welsh

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Completion of screens in Welsh] 4A.3(1) If, after a claim has been issued, a party provides information to the court by using screens completed and submitted in Welsh, the court must send them for translation into English (“the English translation”), and then provide a copy of the English translation to the parties. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > Completion of screens in Welsh] (2) If a party has submitted screens in Welsh, any time period calculated by reference to the date of submission or notification of the completed screens starts on the date on which the court provides the English translation to the party subject to the time period. ## SECTION 5 – PARTIES ACTING IN PERSON – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE ONLINE – GENERAL

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > SECTION 5 – PARTIES ACTING IN PERSON – DEFENDANT’S RESPONSE ONLINE – GENERAL] Application of this Section

## 5.A1 This Section applies only where the parties are acting in person. ## 5.1 Defendant’s response online – when and how to respond

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 5.1 Defendant’s response online – when and how to respond] 5.1-(1) If the defendant decides to respond to the claim and is able to do so online, and unless the parties have agreed a time extension under subparagraph (3), the defendant must respond to the claim by 4pm on the 28 th day after the issue of the claim form. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 5.1 Defendant’s response online – when and how to respond] (2) The defendant responds to the claim by completing the appropriate form or screens (“response form”) and submitting the response form to the court in the appropriate manner, depending on the nature of their response, as set out in Table A. ## TABLE A

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > TABLE A] Nature of response | Appropriate response form to use | How to submit response form (electronically via OCMC website, or in paper copy to Online Civil Money Claims postal address set out in paragraph 2.1(2))

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > TABLE A] Defend the whole of the claim | The relevant defence response screens on the OCMC website | Electronically, using the OCMC website

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > TABLE A] Defend part of the claim/admit part of the claim | The relevant defence response screens on the OCMC website | Electronically, using the OCMC website

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > TABLE A] Nature of response | Appropriate response form to use | How to submit response form (electronically via OCMC website, or in paper copy to Online Civil Money Claims postal address set out in paragraph 2.1(2))

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > TABLE A] Defence and counterclaim | Form N9B | Paper copy to the OCMC postal address

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > TABLE A] Defence and notice of additional claim | Form N9B Defence and Counterclaim (specified amount) | Paper copy to the OCMC postal address

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > TABLE A] Defence and additional claim | Form N9B Defence and Counterclaim (specified amount) | Paper copy to the OCMC postal address

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > TABLE A] Admission | The relevant admission response screens on the OCMC website | Electronically, using the OCMC website

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > TABLE A] (3) The parties may agree an extension of time to respond of up to 28 days in total. The defendant must record on the OCMC website any such agreed extension of time before the expiry of the original 28 day time limit. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > TABLE A] (4) If a time extension has been agreed and recorded under subparagraph, the defendant must respond to the claim using the OCMC website by 4pm on the last day of the agreed extended time. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > TABLE A] (5) If the parties have agreed an extension of time of less than 28 days but then wish to increase the extension up to 28 days in total, the defendant must file an application at the CNBC. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > TABLE A] (6) On receipt of the application under subparagraph (5), the court is to send the claim out of Online Civil Money Claims. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > TABLE A] (7) If at first the defendant had been unable to respond online and had instead contacted the court and been given more time under paragraph 10.1(6) to respond on paper, if the defendant then became able to respond online, the defendant must still submit their completed response form on time. The form is submitted on time if it is received by the court within 28 days after the date that the court sent the paper response form to the defendant, or such longer period up to an additional 28 days as agreed between the parties and as notified to the court. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > TABLE A] (8). The court must tell the claimant when it receives the defendant’s response form. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > TABLE A] (9). If the defendant does not submit the relevant response form to the court on time, the claimant may request a default judgment from the court, and paragraph 11.1 will apply. ## 5.2

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 5.2] (1) This paragraph applies where the defendant wishes to defend the whole of the claim, or defend part and admit part of the claim and will be using the relevant response screens on the OCMC website to make the response. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 5.2] (2) At the same time that the defendant submits the completed response form to the court in accordance with paragraph 5.1, the defendant must also submit their completed online directions questionnaire to the court, to tell the court what requirements the defendant would have, should a court hearing be necessary, including, if the claim appears suitable for the fast track, intermediate track or multi-track, proposed directions. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 5.2] Sub-section A – Introduction

## 6.1(1) This Section applies where the parties are acting in person and if the defendant –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.1(1) This Section applies where the parties are acting in person and if the defendant –] (a) responds online to the court on time; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.1(1) This Section applies where the parties are acting in person and if the defendant –] (b) wishes only to defend the whole of the claim and makes no other response. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.1(1) This Section applies where the parties are acting in person and if the defendant –] (2) Sub-section B applies if –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.1(1) This Section applies where the parties are acting in person and if the defendant –] (a) the claim is a claim for a specified amount of money only not exceeding £10,000 excluding interest. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.1(1) This Section applies where the parties are acting in person and if the defendant –] (3) Sub-section C applies –

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.1(1) This Section applies where the parties are acting in person and if the defendant –] (a) the claim is a claim for a specified amount of money only exceeding £10,000 excluding interest. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.1(1) This Section applies where the parties are acting in person and if the defendant –] (4) Omitted

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.1(1) This Section applies where the parties are acting in person and if the defendant –] (5) Omitted

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.1(1) This Section applies where the parties are acting in person and if the defendant –] Sub-section B – claim not exceeding £10,000 excluding interest and defendant defending the claim

## 6.2(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section B of section 6 applies. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.2(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section B of section 6 applies.] (2) The court must ask the claimant whether they accept  the defendant’s defence, or whether they do not accept it and wish to continue with the claim. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.2(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section B of section 6 applies.] (3) If, within 33 days after being asked by the court, the claimant uses the OCMC website to tell the court that they do not wish to continue with the claim, the claim will be automatically “stayed” (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.2(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section B of section 6 applies.] (4) If the claimant fails to respond online within the 33 days, the court must “stay” the proceedings (as defined). [PRACTICE DIRECTION 51R – ONLINE CIVIL MONEY CLAIMS PILOT > 6.2(1) This paragraph applies when sub-section B of section 6 applies.] (5) If, within 33 days after being asked by the court, the claimant uses the OCMC website to tell the court that they wish to continue with the claim the claimant must, at the same time, also submit their completed online directions questionnaire to the court, to tell the court what requirements the claimant would have, should a court hearing be necessary, including, if the claim appears suitable for the fast track, intermediate track or multi-track, proposed directions.
